guarantees.claim: Each (i,j) slice assigns in_prd[i][j] = {out_prd[i][aes_rot_int(j,4)], prd_i[i][j]} combinatorially, concatenating MSBs from rotated out_prd and LSBs from prd_i.
Generates one aes_sbox instance per (i,j) that drives data_o[i][j], mask_o[i][j], out_prd[i][j], out_req[i][j] from the connected inputs and the SecSBoxImpl parameter.
Each aes_sbox instance's enable en_i is driven as (en == SP2V_HIGH) and out_ack_i as (out_ack == SP2V_HIGH), making handshake control depend on scalar equality checks.

assumptions.claim: en and out_ack are single-bit signals, and SP2V_HIGH equals 1'b1, so that the equality comparisons produce the intended enable and acknowledge semantics.
assumptions.cond: whenever the S-Box instances are active
assumptions.risk: If en or out_ack are wider than 1 bit, the comparisons may always be false, permanently disabling all S-Box instances and breaking the masked datapath.

assumptions.claim: aes_rot_int(j,4) returns a value in [0,3] for j in [0,3] so that out_prd[i][aes_rot_int(j,4)] is a valid index.
assumptions.risk: An out-of-range index could drive X or undefined values on the MSBs of in_prd, corrupting the PRNG mixing and potentially leaking mask information.

assumptions.claim: out_prd[i][*] signals are driven by the corresponding S-Box instances before being used in the in_prd assignment; the schedule ensures out_prd is stable when sampled.
assumptions.risk: If out_prd is not yet valid (e.g., due to cross-instance ordering or startup), in_prd receives unstable or X MSBs, breaking the entropy mixing and potentially exposing secrets.

uncertain_points.claim: The in_prd assignment feeds out_prd (output of aes_sbox) back into prd_i of the same instance. If aes_sbox has a combinational path from prd_i to prd_o, this forms a combinational loop; even if registered, the rotation across instances may violate setup/hold or cause data ordering hazards.
uncertain_points.risk: Combinational loops cause simulation/synthesis mismatches or silicon oscillation; incorrect ordering breaks mask entropy, threatening side-channel resistance.

uncertain_points.claim: in_prd uses out_prd[i][aes_rot_int(j,4)] from a different column instance of the same row. The cross-instance dependency requires careful sequencing to ensure the sourced instance has produced a valid out_prd; otherwise MSBs may be X or stale.
uncertain_points.risk: Invalid or stale entropy MSBs corrupt the masking quality, potentially exposing intermediate state in a security-critical S-Box.

uncertain_points.claim: The signals en and out_ack may be wider than one bit in the actual design; the equality (en == SP2V_HIGH) would then reduce to a single-bit comparison that may not reflect the intended per-instance control and could silently disable the S-Boxes.
uncertain_points.cond: if en or out_ack are not scalar
uncertain_points.risk: Complete loss of S-Box functionality under a valid multi-bit configuration, hiding bugs and breaking the masked cipher.
